[[File:MichelLazard 1987.jpg|thumb]]
{{Short description|French mathematician (1924–1987)}}
'''Michel Paul Lazard''' (5 December 1924 – 15 September 1987) was a French mathematician who worked on the theory of [[Lie group]]s in the context of [[p-adic analysis|{{nowrap|''p''-adic}} analysis]].

== Career and research ==
Born in [[Paris]], Lazard studied at the [[University of Paris]]–[[University of Paris|Sorbonne]], where he obtained his Ph.D. in 1954 under the direction of [[Albert Châtelet]], with thesis titled ''Sur les groupes nilpotents et les anneaux de Lie''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=251730}}</ref> Subsequently he was a professor at the [[University of Poitiers]] and the [[Paris Diderot University|University of Paris 7]]. He died of suicide at the age of 63.

His work took on a life of its own in the hands of [[Daniel Quillen]] in the late 20th century. Quillen's discovery, that a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] Lazard used to classify [[formal group law]]s was [[isomorphic]] to an important ring in [[topology]], led to the subject of [[chromatic homotopy theory]]. Lazard's self-contained treatise on one-dimensional formal groups also gave rise to the field of [[Barsotti–Tate group|''p''-divisible groups]]. His major contributions were:
* The classification of [[p-adic Lie group|''p''-adic Lie groups]]: every ''p''-adic Lie group is a closed [[subgroup]] of <math>{\rm GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)</math>.
* The classification of (1-dimensional commutative) [[formal group]]s.
* The universal formal group law coefficient ring ([[Lazard's universal ring]]) is a [[polynomial ring]].
* The concept of "analyseurs", reinvented by [[J. Peter May]] under the name [[operad]]s.

== Awards and honours ==
In 1958, Lazard was the first recipient of the ''Prix Audin'', named after the young French mathematician [[Maurice Audin]], who had been assassinated in Algeria.<ref>{{cite web|url= 
https://www.association-audin.fr/presentation/|work=association-audin.fr|title=Association Audin|date=19 November 2020 |access-date=11 June 2022|language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Extras/Audin_thesis/|title=Commemoration of Michel Audin's thesis|publisher=University of St Andrews|date=January 2019|access-date=11 June 2022}}</ref> In 1972, he was awarded the [[Prix Poncelet]] by the [[Académie des Sciences]] for his work on [[abstract algebra|algebra]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série A et B|volume=275| date=11 December 1972| pages=133–134| title=Vie Académique: prix et subventions attribuées en 1972|url= https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k5619450s/f24.item}}</ref>
